sec: Ancillary Labs, Thionamides, RAI & Surgical Indications

items.q: Which ancillary laboratory abnormalities are listed under 'Other laboratory findings' in thyrotoxicosis on page 913?
opts: Hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, and isolated amylase elevation
items.exp: Other laboratory findings on page 913: Hyperglycemia, Hypercalcemia, Leucocytosis, ALP ↑, and LFT ↑. (Book p913)

items.q: What is the expected remission rate with anti-thyroid drug therapy in Graves' disease after 12 to 18 months?
items.exp: Under Treatment: Anti-thyroid drugs achieve '60-70% : Remission In 12-18 months'. (Book p913)

items.q: Match the equivalent thionamide doses from the potency equivalence formula on page 913 — 1) Methimazole 2) Carbimazole 3) Propylthiouracil (PTU) … A) 6 mg B) 10 mg C) 100 mg
items.exp: Dose equivalence formula: 'methimazole (6 mg) = Carbimazole (10 mg) = Propylthiouracil (100 mg)'. (Book p913)

items.q: Why is Propylthiouracil (PTU) preferred in pregnancy despite being hepatotoxic?
opts: Increased plasma protein binding reduces transplacental transfer to the fetus
It has an exceptionally long 24-hour half-life
It is an irreversible inhibitor of iodide uptake
It has zero risk of causing maternal agranulocytosis
items.exp: Under Propylthiouracil: 'Preferred in Pregnancy', '↑ Plasma protein binding', and 'Hepatotoxic (Not preferred now)'. (Book p913)

items.q: Compare Carbimazole and Methimazole properties on page 913: I Carbimazole is preferred over PTU, dosed 5 mg TDS daily, with a half-life of 6-8 hours. II Methimazole is an irreversible inhibitor with a 6-hour half-life, but is teratogenic causing aplasia cutis and choanal atresia.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Both statements match the descriptions of Carbimazole and Methimazole on page 913. (Book p913)

items.q: Match the thionamide adverse effect to its clinical status — 1) Rash 2) Agranulocytosis 3) Hepatobiliary / Autoimmune … A) Most common (m/c) side effect B) Most dangerous side effect C) Cholestasis, Drug-induced lupus
items.exp: Side effects: Rash (m/c), Agranulocytosis (most dangerous), Cholestasis, and Drug-induced lupus. (Book p913)

items.q: A 30-year-old woman with Graves' disease started on carbimazole 2 weeks ago presents with high fever, mouth ulcers, and a severe sore throat. What is the most critical and dangerous side effect to rule out immediately?
items.exp: Agranulocytosis is noted as the 'most dangerous' side effect of thionamides; high fever and sore throat require an urgent complete blood count. (Book p913)

items.q: In the titration regimen for antithyroid drugs, the patient should be revisited at ___ weeks to monitor ___ and ___ values.
opts: 4 - 6 weeks; free T3 and free T4
items.exp: Under Titration regimen: 'Revisit : 4-6 weeks, monitor free T3 and free T4 values'. (Book p913)

items.q: What is the recommended dose and schedule of propranolol for thyrotoxic symptom control on page 913?
items.exp: Item 2 under Treatment: 'Propranolol : 40 mg Q6H'. (Book p913)

items.q: Regarding Radioactive Iodine (RAI) in relapsed Graves': I Patient must be made euthyroid with minimum 1 month of antithyroid drugs prior to RAI to prevent thyrotoxic crisis. II RAI has a proven direct association with secondary malignancy risk.
opts: I is true; II is false
Both I and II are true
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Page 913 specifies: 'Before initiating make patient euthyroid: minimum 1 month anti-thyroid drugs (to prevent thyrotoxicosis)' and 'No association with cancer risk'. (Book p913)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a disadvantage or contraindication of radioactive iodine (RAI) on page 913?
opts: High risk of subsequent thyroid carcinoma
Increased risk / aggravation of eye disease
Lifelong L-thyroxine required in 10% of the population
items.exp: Page 913 explicitly notes: 'No association with cancer risk'. Disadvantages listed are C/I in pregnancy, eye disease (↑ risk), and lifelong L-thyroxine required (10%). (Book p913)

items.q: In a patient with Graves' disease and severe, active ophthalmopathy, what medical regimen is recommended on page 913?
opts: Radioactive iodine ablation with high-dose aspirin
Propylthiouracil monotherapy with external cold compresses
Immediate total thyroidectomy preceded by potassium perchlorate
items.exp: Under In relapse cases: 'In Severe Ophthalmopathy : IV Steroid + Rituximab ± Radiotherapy'. (Book p913)

items.q: If radiotherapy is contraindicated or not possible, surgery is indicated for all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: Surgical indications on page 913: biopsy suspicious of malignancy, hyperparathyroidism, pregnancy/lactation, young children, and compressive symptoms. (Book p913)
